overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is a useful localized near-miss: it flags the correct density-selection episode but is too hedged and taxonomically mismatched for primary credit. It improves segment recall while worsening mechanism-first instance precision at the fourth threshold.
main_failure_modes: Near-neighbor labels replace the hidden Stereotyping and Incentive bias labels, producing strict false positives and false negatives despite full mechanism matches.
The Satisficing instance is not identified; it appears only as a hedged anchoring candidate.
Candidate inclusion converts the density-selection segment miss into a segment hit but adds an instance-level false positive.
main_strengths: The two identified findings are accurately localized with valid quotations.
The classification and value-engineering findings capture the hidden mechanisms and reasoning operations fully under the mechanism-first scorecard.
The RAG avoids a false alarm on the deliberately non-biased commissioning segment and does not fabricate retrieval support.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run demonstrates strong mechanism-level detection of two of three biased episodes at moderate confidence, but zero strict taxonomy accuracy because related labels were selected instead of the hidden benchmark labels. Candidate output improves segment coverage without improving primary instance-level performance.
